devices—demonstrate a commitment to complying with legal takedown requests if they were properly issued by the copyright enforcement group.", "summary": "Binnews claims its rapid internal alert system proves it would comply with proper legal takedown notices."}, "9": {"original": "Dvdrs claims they only index files from commercial US hard drives, do not host\u0002", "rephrased": "The Usenet indexing service dvdrs.net argues that it functions as a legitimate directory pointing to files hosted on commercial, tax-paying US-based companies rather than hosting illegal content itself, contending that legal action should be directed exclusively at the actual file hosts instead of the indexing service.", "summary": "dvdrs.net argues it only indexes files from commercial US hosts and should not be sued."}, "10": {"original": "Should the MPAA deem us illegal, they must also target premium paid Usenet\u0002", "rephrased": "The Descds Usenet indexing service contends that if the carriers like Easynews and Usenetserver have not faced similar lawsuits.", "summary": "Descds argues the MPAA must also sue premium Usenet providers if they target Descds."}, "11": {"original": "Descds, despite being outside US jurisdiction, is happy to assist the MPAA in\u0002", "rephrased": "The Descds Usenet indexing service states that despite operating outside US jurisdiction, it is willing to assist the Motion Picture Association in resolving the dispute by removing illegal sections immediately upon receiving a legal judgment, while expressing hope that the organization will communicate directly to avoid unnecessary litigation.", "summary": "Descds offers to assist the MPAA in resolving the dispute despite jurisdictional limits."}}
